purpose: Curated research sources for the interactive Portfolio_LongLeo motion/UI system and its landing/video projects.

selectionPolicy.note: Catalog entries are research references and integration candidates. Do not install or embed a dependency without a separate task, license review and verification.

uxUi: semantic landmarks and clear interaction affordances
content density, empty/error/loading states and focus order
designSystem: consistent type scale, spacing, radius, elevation and motion timing
color: WCAG AA contrast for text and UI states
do not use color as the only status signal
verify dark/light theme pairs and gradient text against their real backgrounds
hoverAndInteraction: hover is enhancement, never the only way to discover or operate a control
focus-visible and pressed states must remain visible
pointer effects must be gated to fine pointers and reduced-motion preference
mobileAndResponsive: touch targets and pointer behavior must survive without hover
images, typography, grids and motion must degrade without horizontal overflow
qaQc: Web Vitals and runtime error checks on representative devices
modalPopup: open and close from every trigger, Escape and backdrop
focus trap, focus restore, aria-expanded and inert background
scroll lock, nested media cleanup and mobile safe-area behavior
embeds: lazy facade before third-party iframe load
allowlisted URL parsing, youtube-nocookie, title and referrer policy
destroy media on close and provide an external-link fallback
fonts: preconnect, font-display swap, weight budget and FOIT/CLS review
same typography contract across portfolio, CV and landing pages
forms: pending, success, error and timeout states
honeypot, length limits, third-party endpoint and privacy review
media: alt text, responsive source selection, lazy/decode and loading fallback
aspect ratio, poster/facade and error state for video/image media
iconsSvgLogos: use semantic inline SVG or an image role appropriate to the meaning of the graphic
preserve viewBox/currentColor, explicit dimensions and visible focus/pressed states for interactive icons
keep decorative SVGs out of the accessibility tree and provide an accessible name for meaningful controls
separate generic UI icon licenses from brand/logo permissions, trademark rules and source-specific guidelines
optimize SVG safely and avoid remote icon-CDN runtime dependencies unless a separate privacy/performance review approves them
seoSocialI18n: canonical, hreflang, title, description, Open Graph and Twitter metadata
language-consistent visible labels, aria labels, CV iframe and dynamic metadata
sitemap, robots, structured data and crawlable project hrefs
browserSupport: feature detection for View Transition, ScrollTimeline and IntersectionObserver
reduced-motion, hidden-tab throttling, autoplay policy and touch/pointer behavior
adaptiveFrameRuntime: treat AFR as an implementation policy, not a browser API: use requestAnimationFrame timestamps and frame-time feedback instead of assuming 60Hz
use an explicit quality ladder such as full, balanced, lite and static; reduce expensive effects before reducing readable content or interaction affordances
combine hard user constraints (prefers-reduced-motion, Save-Data) with soft runtime signals (visibility, intersection, observed long tasks, frame time and supported device/network hints)
pause or stop loops when hidden or off-screen, batch DOM reads/writes, prefer transform/opacity and budget work per frame
feature-detect every signal, avoid user-agent sniffing, expose a manual override where appropriate and record the evidence behind tier changes
lightweightLoading: keep the critical path small: ship only above-the-fold HTML/CSS/fonts/media needed for first paint and defer enhancement code
use loading, decoding, responsive sources, content-visibility and fetchpriority as independent hints with reserved dimensions and measured LCP/CLS impact
schedule non-critical work during idle or with task priorities, and chunk long tasks so input and rendering retain time
gate prefetch and speculative work by same-origin policy, visibility, effective connection and Save-Data; do not spend a user's data budget silently
set explicit byte, request, DOM and animation budgets; validate on low-end mobile and throttled network profiles instead of desktop alone
adaptiveMotionEffects: reduced motion is a hard accessibility mode: remove or replace non-essential movement, parallax, autoplay and repeated effects
adapt quality continuously but hysteretically to avoid oscillation: require consecutive bad/good samples before changing tiers and cool down between changes
preserve semantic state, focus, keyboard operation, contrast and content when disabling blur, particles, tilt, shadows or continuous animation
use CSS media queries for declarative fallbacks and JavaScript only for timers, canvas, audio or third-party effects that CSS cannot stop
verify full, lite, reduced-motion, hidden-tab, slow-network and unsupported-API paths as separate user flows
standardsAndResearch: WCAG 2.2 AA target with WAI-ARIA APG patterns for dialogs and carousels
separate normative requirements, implementation techniques and design references
record evidence, assumptions, date checked and unresolved limitations
privacyAndThirdParty: defer third-party media until user intent where practical
review CSP, referrer policy, Permissions Policy, embeds, fonts and form processors
document public access keys, retention, region and spam/abuse controls
designReference: use design systems for tokens, states, spacing, color and motion vocabulary
adapt patterns to the Portfolio's dark/amber bilingual brand instead of copying a framework
keep design references separate from runtime dependencies
testingAutomation: browser user flows for menus, modals, slider, language, theme and form
automated axe/Lighthouse checks plus manual keyboard, screen-reader and touch review
run checks against visible dynamic states, not only initial HTML

confirmedRelevantSources: accessibility, Lighthouse and Web Vitals references
sheetCoverage.policy: Missing dedicated rows are tracked as implementation contracts, not fabricated Sheet resources.

resources.name: MDN Pointer Events
resources.recommendedUse: Input contract for mouse, touch and pen behavior in interactive cards, canvas hosts and future game surfaces.
resources.risk: Cross-browser pointer, touch and pen behavior still needs device testing.

resources.name: MDN Web Audio API
resources.recommendedUse: Validate audio unlock, user-gesture and buffer behavior before adding sound effects or music.
resources.risk: Autoplay and user-activation policies differ across browsers and devices.

resources.name: MDN Server-sent events
resources.recommendedUse: Choose EventSource for one-way timestamped status updates when a live landing does not need bidirectional control.
resources.risk: Reconnect, proxy buffering, stale state and page-visibility behavior must be handled explicitly.

resources.name: MDN WebSocket API
resources.recommendedUse: Consider only when a landing requires bidirectional low-latency interaction; prefer a simpler request or SSE contract otherwise.
resources.risk: Connection lifecycle, backpressure, reconnect storms and server capacity need an explicit policy.

resources.name: MDN IndexedDB API
resources.recommendedUse: Browser storage contract if the Portfolio later adds local-first drafts, saved filters or offline project data.
resources.risk: Quota and eviction behavior vary; local storage is not a permanent backup.

resources.name: MDN Service Worker API
resources.recommendedUse: Reference for an offline shell only after cache invalidation and update behavior are designed.
resources.risk: Stale-client and cache-update races can make deployments difficult to reason about.

resources.name: axe-core
resources.recommendedUse: Add to browser accessibility checks when a stable browser test harness is available; keep keyboard and screen-reader review alongside it.
resources.risk: Automated checks do not replace keyboard, screen-reader, touch and visual review.

resources.name: Web Vitals
resources.recommendedUse: Use LCP, INP and CLS as release gates for motion-heavy pages and mobile layouts.
resources.risk: Measure on real devices and representative pages; thresholds and context can change.

resources.name: MDN Content Security Policy
resources.recommendedUse: Use to design production headers and validate trusted fonts, images, forms and third-party resources.
resources.risk: Roll out with report-only first; an overly strict policy can break legitimate runtime resources.

resources.name: OWASP ASVS
resources.recommendedUse: Map only relevant controls to forms, headers, public assets, logging and future save/API surfaces.
resources.risk: The standard is broad; this project needs a focused control subset.

resources.name: GSAP documentation
resources.recommendedUse: Reference for timeline, easing, scroll-linked motion and performance decisions; keep the current vanilla implementation unless complexity justifies GSAP.
resources.risk: Review license and bundle cost before any commercial embedding or runtime adoption.

resources.name: GSAP
resources.recommendedUse: Consider only for complex timelines, SVG/canvas choreography or scroll orchestration that native CSS/JS cannot maintain clearly.
resources.risk: Review standard-license terms and avoid adding a dependency for effects the current engine already handles.

resources.name: GSAP Skills
resources.recommendedUse: Use as agent guidance for timelines, ScrollTrigger, performance and reduced-motion decisions; do not ship the skill pack to visitors.
resources.risk: Skill guidance must remain aligned with the actual vanilla architecture and project constraints.

resources.name: Impeccable
resources.recommendedUse: Extract design context, anti-pattern review and repeatable visual QA ideas; do not install its CLI/hooks without a separate trust review.
resources.risk: Node CLI, hooks and browser/local-file access create supply-chain and workflow risk.

resources.name: FFmpeg
resources.recommendedUse: Use for media probe, transcode and export in a dedicated video workflow, not as a browser Portfolio dependency.
resources.risk: LGPL/GPL obligations depend on build configuration; validate argv, resources and codec licensing.

resources.name: OpenTimelineIO
resources.recommendedUse: Use as an editorial interchange contract if a future Portfolio project exposes timeline or render-plan data.
resources.risk: Mappings can be lossy; define the supported subset before exchanging timelines.

resources.name: whisper.cpp
resources.recommendedUse: Reference for local transcription and timestamp generation in a separate media pipeline.
resources.risk: Benchmark model quality, timestamps, language support and weight terms before production use.

resources.name: PySceneDetect
resources.recommendedUse: Reference for detecting scene cuts and transitions before generating or reviewing video deliverables.
resources.risk: Scene detection is not a creative-quality score; keep human review in the loop.

resources.name: c2pa-rs
resources.recommendedUse: Plan as an adapter for signed provenance when generated media becomes part of a production delivery pipeline.
resources.risk: Signing-key handling and privacy require an explicit threat model.

resources.name: Agent Plugins specification
resources.recommendedUse: Reference only if Portfolio tooling later packages reusable skills or MCP adapters; pin versions and validate manifests.
resources.risk: Plugins need version pinning, path containment, trust and permission policies before execution.

resources.name: Using Claude Code: The unreasonable effectiveness of HTML
resources.recommendedUse: Use as a principle for dense, shareable HTML specs, interactive comparisons and visual review artifacts.
resources.risk: Generated HTML can run JavaScript and load external assets; sandbox and review before opening sensitive artifacts.

resources.name: Rớt chữ, rớt dòng — lỗi typography AI không tự sửa cho bạn
resources.recommendedUse: Turn into a Vietnamese typography checklist: line breaks, diacritics, fallback fonts, safe areas and visual hierarchy.
resources.risk: The Sheet records that the article was not fully retrievable; read manually before converting claims into rules.

resources.name: Designer Việt Nam
resources.recommendedUse: Discover Vietnamese typography, Adobe, UI/UX and motion references; verify source, license and malware risk for every download.
resources.risk: Community resources have mixed quality and licensing.

resources.name: Superdesign
resources.recommendedUse: Benchmark prompt-to-UI workflow, design iteration and export quality; do not make it a core runtime dependency.
resources.risk: Hosted pricing, data policy, export quality and generated-design rights require current verification.

resources.name: Ideogram
resources.recommendedUse: Reference text rendering and typography/layout experiments using licensed sample assets only.
resources.risk: Pricing, output rights, API terms and privacy must be verified before production use.

resources.name: MDN Page Visibility API
resources.recommendedUse: Pause/resume expensive loops, media previews and autosave behavior when the tab is hidden.
resources.risk: Background throttling differs across browsers; hidden-tab behavior must be deterministic.

resources.name: Lighthouse
resources.recommendedUse: Use for repeatable performance, accessibility and best-practice audits alongside real-device Web Vitals and manual review.
resources.risk: Scores vary with device/network/environment and are not a complete quality verdict.

resources.name: open-design
resources.recommendedUse: Study local-first design-system, prototype/export and sandboxed preview contracts; do not replace the Portfolio architecture.
resources.risk: Desktop/agent platform scope is much larger than this repo; review sandbox and export boundaries before reuse.

resources.name: ui-ux-pro-max-skill
resources.recommendedUse: Use as a checklist/reference for UI hierarchy, design direction and responsive polish before editing components.
resources.risk: Agent-generated guidance still needs review against the Portfolio's existing tokens, bilingual content and interaction model.

resources.name: morphicons
resources.recommendedUse: Reference icon state transitions and microinteraction vocabulary; prefer semantic buttons and the current no-dependency approach.
resources.risk: Reduced-motion behavior is opt-in in the recorded review; accessibility policy must remain explicit.

resources.name: motion-dev-animations-skill
resources.recommendedUse: Extract animation review vocabulary and recipes, then validate reduced-motion, frame cost and bundle impact in this vanilla codebase.
resources.risk: Skill advice can cause jank or accessibility regressions if copied without target-device testing.

resources.name: tailwindcss-motion
resources.recommendedUse: Reference preset/timing ideas only; the Portfolio does not use Tailwind and should not add it for this purpose.
resources.risk: Tailwind version and license compatibility plus motion overuse need review.

resources.name: Libraries.dev
resources.recommendedUse: Benchmark restrained border, loading, glow and image effects while preserving semantic markup and performance budgets.
resources.risk: React and GPU/bundle cost make direct adoption unsuitable for the current shell; Pro assets have separate terms.

resources.name: PixiJS
resources.recommendedUse: Use as a candidate renderer for an isolated interactive canvas scene, 2D game, data-driven visual or high-volume particle/effect layer where DOM/SVG is no longer efficient; lazy-load it only after the scene is visible.
resources.risk: PixiJS introduces a WebGL/WebGPU canvas, asset loading and ticker lifecycle; it can increase GPU, memory, battery and accessibility cost and should not replace the portfolio's DOM/CSS motion layer by default.

resources.name: Font Awesome
resources.recommendedUse: Reference icon sizing, SVG semantics and icon-font trade-offs; keep the current inline SVG/no-dependency approach unless a concrete need appears.
resources.risk: Icon fonts can add payload and accessibility ambiguity; review license and prefer labeled SVG controls.

resources.name: lazysizes
resources.recommendedUse: Benchmark lazy image/iframe loading behavior against the current native loading, srcset and facade implementation; do not add it automatically.
resources.risk: A dependency is unnecessary unless native loading fails a measured requirement; verify browser behavior first.

resources.name: Responsively App
resources.recommendedUse: Use as a manual multi-viewport QA reference for desktop, 390px and 320px layouts when a local browser harness is available.
resources.risk: Desktop tooling does not replace real-device touch, keyboard, screen-reader and performance checks.

resources.name: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.2
resources.recommendedUse: Set WCAG 2.2 AA as the accessibility review target for full responsive pages, dialogs, forms, motion and media.
resources.risk: Conformance requires testing the full page and all responsive variations; automated checks are not sufficient.

resources.name: WAI-ARIA APG Dialog Modal Pattern
resources.recommendedUse: Validate dialog labeling, focus movement, Tab trap, Escape, close control, inert background and focus restoration.
resources.risk: aria-modal must match actual behavior; marking a non-modal implementation modal harms assistive technology users.

resources.name: WAI-ARIA APG Carousel Pattern
resources.recommendedUse: Validate carousel region labeling, slide picker buttons, rotation controls, aria-live policy and auto-rotation behavior.
resources.risk: Auto-rotation must pause on interaction and should not create unexpected announcements or motion.

resources.name: W3C H102 HTML dialog technique
resources.recommendedUse: Compare the custom modal manager against native dialog behavior and focus-order tests before any migration.
resources.risk: W3C techniques are informative examples, not a substitute for testing the actual implementation.

resources.name: MDN HTMLDialogElement
resources.recommendedUse: Evaluate native showModal/close/cancel behavior and inert background support against the current custom animated modal.
resources.risk: Native dialog animation and existing CSS contracts need browser testing before replacement.

resources.name: MDN iframe reference
resources.recommendedUse: Review iframe title, loading, referrerpolicy, allow, sandbox and Permissions Policy decisions for YouTube/CV embeds.
resources.risk: Restrictive iframe policies can break legitimate content; validate the minimum required permissions.

resources.name: MDN prefers-reduced-motion
resources.recommendedUse: Gate scroll, cursor, tilt, carousel and transition effects while preserving content and operability.
resources.risk: A CSS-only rule is not enough when JavaScript timers, requestAnimationFrame or third-party motion are active.

resources.name: MDN CSS scroll-driven animations
resources.recommendedUse: Reference native scroll timelines for progress/reveal effects and retain a feature-detected fallback.
resources.risk: Support and interaction behavior vary; do not remove the fallback path without browser evidence.

resources.name: MDN View Transition API
resources.recommendedUse: Keep view transitions progressive and disabled when reduced motion is requested.
resources.risk: Feature support and transition lifecycle differ by browser; preserve the plain DOM update fallback.

resources.name: MDN Content Security Policy
resources.recommendedUse: Design a report-only then enforced CSP for scripts, styles, fonts, images, frames and the Web3Forms endpoint.
resources.risk: An incomplete policy can break the site or create a false sense of security; deploy headers only after inventorying origins.

resources.name: YouTube Embedded Players and Player Parameters
resources.recommendedUse: Validate video/playlist URLs, autoplay, playsinline, rel, captions, minimum viewport and future IFrame API controls.
resources.risk: Autoplay can trigger data collection on load; only load the player after user intent and review YouTube policy changes.

resources.name: Google Fonts API getting started
resources.recommendedUse: Validate font-display swap, fallback families, subset/weight requests and font request budget for Vietnamese text.
resources.risk: Hosted fonts add third-party requests and privacy/performance considerations; consider self-hosting only after licensing and metrics review.

resources.name: Web3Forms API reference
resources.recommendedUse: Validate browser-side POST, access_key, response codes, email field, subject and timeout/error handling.
resources.risk: The endpoint is an external processor; verify production domain approval, rate limits and privacy disclosure.

resources.name: Web3Forms spam protection
resources.recommendedUse: Review honeypot, server-side spam checks, hCaptcha/Turnstile options and abuse monitoring.
resources.risk: A honeypot alone is not a complete abuse strategy; avoid collecting more personal data than needed.

resources.name: web.dev Optimize Cumulative Layout Shift
resources.recommendedUse: Reserve image/embed space, size images, review web-font shifts and keep motion on transform/opacity where possible.
resources.risk: Lab Lighthouse results do not replace field data from real devices and representative flows.

resources.name: web.dev Learn Images
resources.recommendedUse: Review width/height, srcset/sizes, art direction, formats, lazy loading, decoding and alt text contracts.
resources.risk: Native lazy loading does not replace image dimension, error, crop and content-priority decisions.

resources.name: web.dev high-performance CSS animations
resources.recommendedUse: Review frame cost, compositor-friendly properties, paint/layout triggers and animation debugging.
resources.risk: GPU promotion is not free; verify memory, battery and low-end mobile behavior.

resources.name: web.dev Interaction to Next Paint
resources.recommendedUse: Measure responsiveness of filters, modals, language/theme switches, slider gestures and form submission states.
resources.risk: A single lab run is not representative; pair field and user-flow measurements.

resources.name: Lighthouse documentation
resources.recommendedUse: Run repeatable audits for performance, accessibility, best practices and SEO after browser interaction flows are stable.
resources.risk: Scores depend on environment and throttling; treat them as evidence, not a complete quality verdict.

resources.name: Playwright accessibility testing guide
resources.recommendedUse: Automate visible-state flows and combine Playwright with axe-core, then retain manual review for issues automation cannot detect.
resources.risk: Automated accessibility catches only a subset of WCAG issues; it must not replace keyboard, screen-reader and inclusive user testing.

resources.name: Playwright
resources.recommendedUse: Consider as a future cross-browser test harness for Chromium, Firefox and WebKit; do not add dependency without a separate setup task.
resources.risk: Browser downloads and test infrastructure expand repository/tooling scope; keep runtime portfolio dependency-free.

resources.name: web-vitals repository
resources.recommendedUse: Consider deferred field measurement for LCP, INP, CLS and diagnostic attribution after privacy/analytics policy is defined.
resources.risk: Telemetry is an external data collection decision; do not add it silently or without an endpoint and retention policy.

resources.name: Material Design 3 Foundations
resources.recommendedUse: Benchmark foundations for tokens, accessibility, layout, interaction states, typography and theming without importing Material UI.
resources.risk: The Portfolio has its own dark/amber identity; copying a product system wholesale would create visual and implementation drift.

resources.name: Material Design 3 Motion
resources.recommendedUse: Use motion tokens and spatial/effects vocabulary to keep animation purposeful and consistent.
resources.risk: Physics and expressive motion need reduced-motion alternatives and low-end device validation.

resources.name: IBM Carbon Design System overview
resources.recommendedUse: Benchmark token layers for color, type, spacing, icons, motion, theming and accessibility documentation.
resources.risk: Carbon is a product system, not a dependency target for this vanilla portfolio.

resources.name: IBM Carbon color guidelines
resources.recommendedUse: Use semantic color and layering-token ideas to review dark/light surfaces, text, borders, overlays and states.
resources.risk: Token names and palettes must be adapted to the actual amber/dark contrast evidence in this repository.

resources.name: Radix Dialog accessibility reference
resources.recommendedUse: Benchmark focus trap, trigger focus restore, title/description, inert overlay and Escape behavior without adding React/Radix.
resources.risk: Radix is a React component system and cannot be dropped into this vanilla runtime without changing architecture.

resources.name: Lenis
resources.recommendedUse: Maintain the pinned local vendor with reduced-motion gating, iframe limitations and nested scroll behavior documented.
resources.risk: The current site vendors a local minified file; version drift, smooth-scroll accessibility and iframe interaction require periodic review.

resources.name: Motion reduced-motion guidance
resources.recommendedUse: Cross-check reduced-motion product behavior and animation fallback vocabulary; adapt to vanilla matchMedia code.
resources.risk: The source is React-oriented and must not introduce a framework dependency into the Portfolio.

resources.name: W3C SVG 2
resources.recommendedUse: Use as the platform reference for viewBox, paths, styling, animation, embedded SVG and interactive SVG behavior before creating custom marks or effects.
resources.risk: SVG 2 is a Candidate Recommendation Snapshot; check browser support for newer features and keep the production subset conservative.

resources.name: W3C Accessibility Features of SVG
resources.recommendedUse: Review titles, descriptions, text alternatives, focusability, keyboard behavior and the distinction between decorative and meaningful SVG graphics.
resources.risk: Assistive-technology exposure can vary by browser and SVG embedding mode; verify representative browsers and screen readers manually.

resources.name: MDN SVG reference
resources.recommendedUse: Use for browser-facing SVG syntax, embedding, styling, DOM APIs, animation and compatibility details when implementing custom inline marks or effects.
resources.risk: MDN documents platform behavior but does not grant permission to reuse a third-party logo or icon asset.

resources.name: SVGO SVG Optimizer
resources.recommendedUse: Benchmark safe SVG cleanup and minification for owned icons, logos and illustrations after preserving viewBox, IDs, accessibility metadata and animation hooks.
resources.risk: Aggressive optimization can remove IDs, titles, descriptions, CSS hooks or animation attributes; keep a source SVG and review visual/behavioral diffs.

resources.name: Lucide Icons
resources.recommendedUse: Reference a consistent stroke-based UI icon language and inline-SVG conventions for navigation, controls and service cards; keep only the needed assets if adopted.
resources.risk: Adding a library changes the visual language and payload; verify license, tree-shaking or asset-copy strategy, accessible names and reduced-motion behavior.

resources.name: Heroicons
resources.recommendedUse: Compare outline/solid icon variants, sizing and state treatment for high-salience controls without adopting Tailwind or a framework.
resources.risk: The icon set is MIT but each copied asset still needs attribution/license records as required by the repository and must pass the Portfolio's contrast and labeling checks.

resources.name: Tabler Icons
resources.recommendedUse: Reference a broad MIT-licensed SVG set with outline/filled variants and raw SVG distribution for project controls, media and product sections.
resources.risk: The breadth can create inconsistent icon weights; select one family/size contract and do not add the webfont when inline SVG is sufficient.

resources.name: Phosphor Icons
resources.recommendedUse: Study a multi-weight icon system for expressive portfolio states, while selecting a small consistent subset and mapping weight to semantic emphasis.
resources.risk: Multiple weights can increase visual noise and payload; validate stroke/fill contrast, target size and focus states before adoption.

resources.name: Radix Icons
resources.recommendedUse: Reference a compact 15x15 control-icon vocabulary and restrained UI geometry for menus, dialogs, navigation and form states.
resources.risk: The default grid is small and React-oriented in its official distribution; adapt SVG assets to the vanilla markup without importing React packages.

resources.name: Google Material Design Icons
resources.recommendedUse: Use as a secondary reference for familiar system icons, optical sizing and filled/outlined variants; do not mix families casually with the custom amber visual language.
resources.risk: Material variants can look generic or conflict with the Portfolio's custom icon vocabulary; review license notices and avoid loading the entire icon font.

resources.name: Simple Icons brand SVG library
resources.recommendedUse: Use as a discovery and consistency reference for technology, platform and social brand marks used in project/tool sections; prefer the brand owner's official asset when available.
resources.risk: The project license does not automatically settle the trademark or individual icon license for every brand; check each icon's source, license and brand guidelines before publishing.

resources.name: Simple Icons license and trademark disclaimer
resources.recommendedUse: Use as the mandatory pre-publication checklist for individual logo licenses, trademark ownership, source URLs and permission boundaries.
resources.risk: License and guideline data can change; record the checked date and recheck the exact brand asset before release.

resources.name: Simple Icons brand-source contribution guidance
resources.recommendedUse: Use to trace a logo back to official brand assets and guidelines instead of treating an aggregator copy as the authority.
resources.risk: A source link is evidence of provenance, not a blanket permission to alter, recolor or imply endorsement by the brand.

resources.name: MDN requestAnimationFrame
resources.recommendedUse: Use the browser timestamp for time-based motion, assume display refresh rates vary, and let hidden documents pause naturally before adding explicit lifecycle guards.
resources.risk: requestAnimationFrame is one-shot and refresh-rate synchronized; frame pacing still depends on main-thread work and does not prove a stable FPS target.

resources.name: MDN Network Information API
resources.recommendedUse: Use effectiveType, downlink, rtt or saveData as optional hints for prefetch, media quality and effect tiers, always behind feature detection.
resources.risk: Support is limited and values are estimates; never use this API as the only accessibility or content decision, and avoid treating it as a stable identity signal.

resources.name: MDN Device Memory API
resources.recommendedUse: Use navigator.deviceMemory only as a coarse, optional signal for conservative image, canvas and effect defaults on memory-constrained devices.
resources.risk: The value is coarse, unavailable in several browsers and privacy-reduced; pair it with runtime evidence and never hide essential content because of it.

resources.name: MDN PerformanceObserver
resources.recommendedUse: Observe supported paint, long-task, layout-shift and interaction entries to feed diagnostics or conservative quality changes without sampling every frame.
resources.risk: Entry types and buffering vary by browser; telemetry can add privacy and data-retention obligations, so keep measurement local or explicitly governed.

resources.name: MDN requestIdleCallback
resources.recommendedUse: Schedule non-critical enhancement, prefetch preparation and cleanup during idle time with a timeout and a setTimeout fallback.
resources.risk: Idle time may never arrive under sustained load; it is not suitable for input-critical or render-critical work without a deadline.

resources.name: MDN Prioritized Task Scheduling API
resources.recommendedUse: Use scheduler.postTask priorities as progressive enhancement for user-blocking, user-visible and background tasks, with a portable fallback.
resources.risk: Browser support and priority semantics vary; a priority hint cannot repair a long synchronous task or justify unbounded work.

resources.name: web.dev Fetch Priority
resources.recommendedUse: Use fetchpriority as a narrow browser hint: high only for the true LCP/critical asset and low for deferred carousel or non-critical work, while keeping preload and loading decisions separate.
resources.risk: It is a hint rather than a directive; overusing high priority can compete with CSS, fonts and the actual critical path.

resources.name: web.dev content-visibility
resources.recommendedUse: Evaluate content-visibility: auto for large below-the-fold sections while preserving contain-intrinsic-size, anchors, focus behavior and reveal semantics.
resources.risk: Skipping rendering can affect measurement, find-in-page, focus and scroll anchoring; verify actual pages and do not apply it to critical content blindly.

resources.name: web.dev Optimize long tasks
resources.recommendedUse: Break work into smaller tasks, yield between chunks and keep input/rendering responsive before attempting FPS or effect-level tuning.
resources.risk: Chunking has overhead and can complicate ordering; measure task duration and interaction impact rather than optimizing arbitrary function counts.

resources.name: web.dev Optimize Interaction to Next Paint
resources.recommendedUse: Use INP-oriented guidance to review pointer, keyboard, modal, filter, theme and language interactions before adding effects or adaptive scheduling.
resources.risk: Lab timing is not field evidence; pair repeatable flows with real-device and field measurement when telemetry is approved.

resources.name: GoogleChromeLabs quicklink
resources.recommendedUse: Study viewport-aware, idle-time, same-origin and connection-aware prefetching for static multi-page navigation; prefer the pattern before adopting the library.
resources.risk: Prefetch can waste bandwidth or expose routes; respect Save-Data, slow connections, origin allowlists and explicit user intent.

resources.name: fastdom
resources.recommendedUse: Reference a measure/mutate batching model that separates layout reads from writes when custom motion code grows beyond a small rAF loop.
resources.risk: A scheduler does not remove layout cost or fix incorrect lifecycle cleanup; the current vanilla site should adopt the pattern only after a measured need.

resources.name: Tempus shared animation frame manager
resources.recommendedUse: Compare one shared rAF clock, target-FPS throttling and per-callback frame budgets when evaluating an AFR architecture.
resources.risk: It is a library and patching global rAF can conflict with existing vendors; keep the portfolio's local loop explicit unless profiling justifies migration.

resources.name: pmndrs scheduler
resources.recommendedUse: Study dependency-aware jobs, a shared frame loop, delta time and frame-budget decisions for canvas or simulation work without importing React.
resources.risk: The scheduler solves ordering, not visual design or accessibility; do not apply game-loop complexity to ordinary DOM interactions.

resources.name: Vercel Phase lifecycle-aware UI performance layer
resources.recommendedUse: Study lifecycle contracts that pause off-screen/background work, respect reduced motion, share clocks and defer non-critical rendering.
resources.risk: The repository is alpha and React-oriented; use its principles as research, not as permission to add a framework or unstable runtime dependency.

resources.name: Cloudflare web-perf agent skill
resources.recommendedUse: Borrow the audit workflow for loading bottlenecks and Core Web Vitals while keeping the report honest about measured versus unmeasured evidence.
resources.risk: Cloudflare-specific recommendations may not apply to this Vercel/static deployment; inspect skill files before installation and never execute bundled scripts blindly.

resources.name: Mapbox web performance patterns skill
resources.recommendedUse: Review a skill packaging model for web-performance patterns, then adapt only general loading/rendering lessons to this vanilla portfolio.
resources.risk: The skill is Mapbox-focused and may contain project-specific assumptions; treat third-party agent instructions as untrusted until reviewed.

resources.name: Zero-Jank Scroll Agent Skill
resources.recommendedUse: Use its quality-contract ideas for scroll-driven motion: architecture choice, reduced-motion, responsive fallback, cleanup and runtime evidence.
resources.risk: Third-party skills can contain unsafe or irrelevant operational instructions; review SKILL.md and scripts before any installation or execution.

resources.name: Three.js
resources.recommendedUse: Reference or prototype optional 3D/WebGL/WebGPU scenes for dedicated landing pages; keep the main portfolio CSS/DOM-first and lazy-load any renderer behind capability and visibility checks.
resources.risk: WebGL/WebGPU adds GPU, memory, battery and accessibility cost plus a second render loop; do not add it to the initial homepage without a measured product need and fallback.

resources.name: Anime.js
resources.recommendedUse: Reference or isolate for multi-step DOM/SVG/object timelines, stagger and path animation where the current custom motion engine becomes hard to maintain.
resources.risk: A second animation scheduler can conflict with the existing CSS/rAF/Lenis system; add only after profiling, gate reduced motion manually, and avoid controlling the same element from two engines.

resources.name: Animate.css
resources.recommendedUse: Study small CSS entrance/attention patterns and reduced-motion handling; reimplement selected keyframes with the portfolio's own tokens instead of importing the full stylesheet.
resources.risk: The current project license is Hippocratic License and the full library duplicates existing animations.css; review license compatibility and payload before copying any code.

resources.name: Android AnimatedVectorDrawable
resources.recommendedUse: Reference native vector path and group animations for Android TV or companion app work; use it to keep icon transitions vector-based and remote-friendly.
resources.risk: It is Android-native and does not belong in this static web runtime; coordinate timing and reduced-motion behavior separately if a web analogue is designed.

resources.name: Android Animatable2
resources.recommendedUse: Reference lifecycle callbacks for native drawable animation completion and repeat handling when designing Android TV motion contracts.
resources.risk: The API applies to Android Drawable implementations, not DOM/CSS; do not port its lifecycle assumptions into the portfolio without an explicit adapter and tests.

resources.name: Morphicons
resources.recommendedUse: Reference morphing icon semantics and showcase patterns alongside the Morphicons source repository.
resources.risk: Review the actual asset license and implementation cost before copying icon artwork or adding it to the shared icon layer.

resources.name: AniBox ecosystem live site
resources.recommendedUse: Featured project reference for a remote-first Android TV product: adaptive media UI, install/update flows, public roadmap and transparent usage metrics.
resources.risk: The live product, release version and metrics change over time; describe the project at a high level and link to the live source instead of hard-coding volatile release claims.

resources.name: AniBox release repository
resources.recommendedUse: Link the public release/source surface for AniBox from the portfolio's open-source projects section.
resources.risk: This repository may expose release artifacts rather than the complete application source; do not infer implementation details beyond its published contents.

resources.name: Kern LanyardPass Framer component
resources.recommendedUse: Study a tactile pass/lanyard interaction: rope physics, Three.js canvas composition, configurable card content, lighting and reduced-motion handling; adapt the interaction contract rather than copying the Framer module into this vanilla site.
resources.risk: The module imports React, Framer, Framer Motion and Three.js and loads remote demo assets; it is not a drop-in dependency for this static portfolio and needs an asset, license and performance review.

resources.name: React Three Fiber
resources.recommendedUse: Reference declarative Three.js scene composition, useFrame-style render-loop participation and ecosystem patterns for a future React-based product or isolated prototype.
resources.risk: R3F is a React renderer and pairs with React major versions; adding it to this framework-free portfolio would introduce React, Three.js and a bundler rather than extending the current vanilla AFR directly.

resources.name: Framer free components marketplace
resources.recommendedUse: Use as a visual research source for interaction patterns, component states and motion references; reimplement selected ideas with local tokens and the portfolio's accessibility/performance contract.
resources.risk: Marketplace components vary in code quality, dependencies, licensing and remote asset behavior; do not import or hotlink a component without reviewing its source, license and runtime cost.

resources.name: Tencent BrowserSkill
resources.recommendedUse: Evaluate as an alternative visible-browser connector for authorized QA and logged-in workflows; compare its bsk CLI/extension model with the ORCA browser-harness already available.
resources.risk: It can operate a real logged-in Chrome/Edge profile and retain debugging evidence; install only after reviewing extension permissions, profile boundaries, redaction and daemon ownership. Do not run its remote install script blindly.

resources.name: Browser Use
resources.recommendedUse: Reference Python browser-agent orchestration, Playwright/CDP integration and evaluation patterns for a separate QA or research service.
resources.risk: It is a Python/agent/cloud stack with model, browser-session and credential concerns; it does not belong in this static portfolio runtime and may overlap with ORCA browser tools.

resources.name: Workflow Use
resources.recommendedUse: Study deterministic, self-healing browser workflows and recorder-to-workflow ideas for repeatable QA scenarios.
resources.risk: The repository is explicitly early development and AGPL-3.0; do not copy it into a closed portfolio toolchain without a license review, and do not rely on it for production automation yet.

resources.name: Browser Use Browser Harness
resources.recommendedUse: Use the existing ORCA browser-harness skill for HTTP-served portfolio QA, console checks, screenshots and interaction evidence when the local Chrome CDP connection is available.
resources.risk: It controls a real browser profile and may expose signed-in state to authorized actions; never print cookies/tokens and stop when DevTools/connection consent is missing.

resources.name: Video Use
resources.recommendedUse: Reference or selectively use for authorized video editing workflows: filler/dead-space cuts, FFmpeg chains, subtitles and animation overlay generation.
resources.risk: It is a separate Python/FFmpeg agent workflow and can overwrite or process media; keep it outside the portfolio runtime and review input/output paths before execution.

resources.name: Jev Ultrafast
resources.recommendedUse: Study indexed action spaces, compact element tables and benchmark methodology for faster browser QA agents.
resources.risk: The repository is small/research-oriented and its speed claims depend on cloud/model/browser conditions; do not treat it as a production replacement for ORCA browser-harness.
